# RiteSmith

> RiteSmith is the missing layer between LLM planning and deterministic execution.

## What it does

Most agent systems put the LLM in the critical path of every step — think, act, observe, repeat. RiteSmith breaks that loop:

- The **LLM / Agent** understands intent and submits it to RiteSmith
- **RiteSmith** searches existing artifacts, generates missing Lua capabilities and workflow definitions, validates them under guardrails (schema, policy, sandbox), and registers them in the artifact registry
- **Trama** executes the resulting workflow with retries, durable state, sleep, callbacks, compensation, and observability

RiteSmith is a **generator**, not an executor. It does not run workflows. Trama does.

## Core concepts

- **Intent** — a structured request submitted by an LLM or agent describing what needs to happen
- **Artifact registry** — the store of reusable Lua capabilities and workflow definitions that RiteSmith searches before generating new ones
- **Guardrails** — schema validation, policy checks, and sandbox execution that RiteSmith applies before registering any artifact
- **Workflow definition** — a declaristic description of steps, dependencies, and compensation logic that Trama can execute
- **Lua capabilities** — lightweight, sandboxed functions that represent executable actions within a workflow

## What RiteSmith is not

- Not an LLM wrapper or prompt framework
- Not a workflow engine (Trama is the engine)
- Not an agent loop (it eliminates the loop)

## Relationship to Trama

RiteSmith is built on top of [Trama](https://trama.run), a lightweight saga orchestrator for reliable distributed workflows. Trama provides durable workflow state, retries, compensation, callbacks, and production-grade execution semantics.
